key_insight: Full transfer onto a ~1.6 fF floating diffusion plus CDS reads ~1,000-electron packets cleanly; writes go through a transistor channel, so endurance is unlimited.
killer_doubt: Duplicate of I-00973. Planar pinned well holds ~6,000 e-/um2: 1,000 e- plus 3-4T is ~0.2 um2, ~50-90x a 1-beta bit; 85 C hot-pixel tails give ~10 ms.
decisive_experiment: None separate: settled by the I-00973 CIS-MPW test chip (fill-and-spill electrical write, 25 ns CDS read, dark-current tails at 25-85 C).
prior_art: Global-shutter CIS pinned in-pixel storage nodes; Fossum/Ma pump-gate jots; our Phase B N-84 Jot-RAM; 1970s CCD memories.

key_insight: Pinning moves stored electrons off every Si/SiO2 interface: median dark current ~0.1-5 e-/s at 25-60 C, >1e4x below a 13 fA (8e4 e-/s) tail, with channel-written charge.
killer_doubt: Planar cell is ~0.1-0.2 um2/bit (50-90x 1-beta). A 40 nm vertical well needs ~2-3e18 cm-3 doping at 0.5-1 MV/cm, where tunnelling erases the dark-current advantage.
decisive_experiment: 65-110 nm CIS MPW (~$300k): pinned wells 0.1-0.5 um wide with fill-and-spill electrical write and 25 ns CDS column read; measure transfer lag, write accuracy and dark-current tails at 25-85 C versus width.
prior_art: CIS global-shutter pinned storage nodes; Fossum QIS jots (0.1 e-/s); our N-84 Jot-RAM is the vertical, multi-level version.

key_insight: Clean, backed-up pages can trade refresh for detection: Linux already drops and re-reads clean page-cache pages on uncorrectable errors, so slow-refresh banks need little new software.
killer_doubt: At 4 s and 85 C, BER ~9e-4 makes ~64% of 4 KB pages fail SECDED; 1 s works, but TRR rides REF commands, so hammer exposure rises ~16x.
decisive_experiment: DRAM-Bender FPGA on 30 DDR5 dies (~$150k): SECDED-fail rate versus refresh interval (64 ms-4 s, 45-85 C) and HCfirst versus interval; then a kernel patch mapping clean page cache to slow banks.
prior_art: Flikker (ASPLOS 2011) per-bank slow refresh for non-critical data; Smart Refresh skips recently activated rows; Linux hwpoison clean-page recovery.

key_insight: One retention atlas versus temperature and bias measures the tail's activation energy and field mechanism, which decides N-42 (3x or 18x from cooling), N-63 and this batch's refresh ideas.
killer_doubt: Standalone payoff is small: vendors already do internal failure analysis, and if tail Ea is ~0.2-0.3 eV (GIDL/TAT), cooling 85 to 35 C buys only ~3-5x.
decisive_experiment: FPGA testers and thermal chambers on ~100 DDR4/DDR5/LPDDR5 dies from three vendors (~$300k): per-cell retention at 25-95 C and three wordline-low biases; extract Ea and field-enhancement histograms across the 1e-9 to 1e-5 tail.
prior_art: Hamamoto 1998 retention activation energies; Umeda et al. 2006 EDMR linked VRT to a vacancy-oxygen defect; SAFARI retention studies (Liu 2013, REAPER 2017).

key_insight: Zero-hardware refresh relief is real: 4x tREFI cuts refresh energy ~75% and recovers most of the 7.6-20% tRFC bandwidth loss if weak pages are mapped out.
killer_doubt: VRT cells keep appearing after profiling; a 4x window gives hammer 4x more ACTs; 0.05% of 16M pages is ~8k entries (~25 KB), far beyond 384 B user SPD.
decisive_experiment: On 20 ECC servers with exposed tREFI, profile at 4x, retire failing pages, then log corrected and uncorrected errors for 90 days at 45-85 C; kill if new weak pages exceed ~1e-6 per day.
prior_art: RAIDR (2012), REAPER reach profiling (2017), AVATAR ECC-triggered row upgrade (2015), BadRAM; overclockers already run maximum tREFI.

key_insight: Matching memory lifetime to data lifetime is sound, and oxide TFTs need no EUV; a cheap, slow, deliberately leaky tier for transient AI data is a legitimate product shape.
killer_doubt: Steel foil (10-17 ppm/K) moves 3-5 um per kelvin over 30 cm, ~100x a 30 nm overlay budget for 100 nm TFTs. Activations live 0.1-10 s, not 1-10 ms.
decisive_experiment: Measure layer-to-layer overlay of two nanoimprint levels across a 30 cm roll-to-roll web on a pilot line (~$100k); kill if 3-sigma overlay exceeds ~30 nm, then test IGZO 1T1C retention at 100 nm.
prior_art: HP SAIL self-aligned roll-to-roll imprint TFTs; PragmatIC/Arm PlasticARM flexible IGZO processor with on-chip RAM (2021); display-fab oxide TFT panels.

key_insight: Never storing regenerable data is the cheapest memory: a seeded generator near memory trades a few pJ of compute for capacity and bandwidth.
killer_doubt: Seed-regenerable tensors are <1% of AI memory; trained weights and KV are not. FlashAttention already regenerates dropout masks; VeRA and NOLA already seed LoRA bases.
decisive_experiment: Audit peak memory of five production training and inference jobs by tensor class (~$20k of compute); kill if seed-regenerable tensors are under 2% of peak bytes.
prior_art: FlashAttention dropout regeneration from Philox state; VeRA, NOLA and PRANC seeded random bases; RoPE computed on the fly.

key_insight: Refresh need not chase the 1e-9 tail: flipped cells stay flipped under internal refresh, so raw BER stays bounded and a page-level code can absorb it.
killer_doubt: Refresh costs 46 fJ x 15.6/s = 0.72 pJ/bit/s; LDPC decode ~1 pJ/bit per read, so any bit read over ~once per second loses. Weights are read 10-50x/s.
decisive_experiment: Replay FPGA-measured error maps at 1-8 s intervals through hard-decision LDPC and BCH models; compare decode energy times read rate against refresh energy saved, using HBM inference traces (~$100k).
prior_art: Hi-ECC (Wilkerson, ISCA 2010) multi-bit 1 KB codes to stretch eDRAM refresh; our N-63 scrub-as-refresh at BER ~1e-5 with lazy syndrome dominates.

key_insight: A 1.5 eV-activated series element gives ~1e10 on/off between 85 C and 400 C with no transistor: a two-terminal crossbar cell whose gate is temperature.
killer_doubt: A hot row at 1% duty sees 7e13 x 10 ns: ~8 days cumulative at 400 C. Heating ~1-5 pJ/cell makes a row ~10-40 nJ versus ~2 nJ ACT.
decisive_experiment: Fabricate heater-gated MIM test structures in a university fab (~$200k); measure the conductance Arrhenius slope at 25-450 C and retention at 85 C, then apply 1e10 ns heat pulses and track drift.
prior_art: Thermally assisted switching MRAM (Crocus) and HAMR use heat as the write gate; PCM ns heaters. None found for charge-storage access.

key_insight: Any refresh relaxation needs hammer protection decoupled from REF commands; one per-row debt that resets on any restore is the natural way to unify them.
killer_doubt: By the 85 C tail model, 4x interval leaves ~1.5% of rows weak, 8x ~11%. PRAC already counts per-row ACTs; additivity of hammer and leakage loss is unmeasured.
decisive_experiment: DRAM-Bender on 20 DDR4/DDR5 dies (~$150k): measure HCfirst versus time since victim refresh (0-100% of retention) at 50 and 85 C; the debt model holds if HCfirst falls linearly with elapsed fraction.
prior_art: JEDEC DDR5 PRAC per-row activation counters; RAIDR retention bins; RowPress shows aggressor on-time matters, so ACT counts alone are incomplete.

key_insight: One hole etch and no per-bit transistor or capacitor: CCD-clocked NAND word planes give ~1.8-3.7 Gb/mm2 (4-8x 1-beta) at single-exposure ArF, with channel-written charge and unlimited endurance.
killer_doubt: 180 transfers per circulation needs CTE >=0.99994; ~250 e- packets against ~10-90 traps per gate leave poly or amorphous channels near 0.999. Cost is ~2-3x below DRAM, not 100x.
decisive_experiment: University-fab planar overlapping-gate IGZO CCD, plus a buried-channel bilayer variant, with 16-32 gates (~$300k): CTE versus clock (1-100 MHz), fat zero and temperature to 85 C; build vertical stacks only if >=0.9999.
prior_art: 1970s serial CCD memories (Intel, Fairchild); our Phase B N-08 vertical oxide CCD; no vertical-CCD memory patent found (via search snippet).

key_insight: Optical tier select would remove staircase contacts and per-tier masks, the cost that grows fastest as 3D stacks get taller.
killer_doubt: QDs absorb every photon above their gap, so short wavelengths excite all lower-gap tiers. A guiding light pipe needs a core >=~300 nm, against ~40 nm column pitch.
decisive_experiment: Stack three QD photoconductor films with distinct gaps in a university lab (~$100k); measure cross-tier photocurrent selectivity per wavelength and dark leakage at 85 C; kill if selectivity is below 100:1.
prior_art: Wavelength-multiplexed optical and holographic storage addressing; resonant-cavity photodetectors. None found for 3D DRAM tier select.
